articles.title: Physical AI Needs a Neuromorphic Path from Sensor to Silicon - EE Times
articles.summary:
The physical world does not wait for a sampling clock. It changes, moves, touches, slips, and vibrates continuously, yet the information that matters is often sparse, unpredictable, and fleeting.
A robot needs to react when an object approaches. A gripper needs to know the instant contact is made or slip begins. Yet much of today’s sensing and AI stack still samples physical signals at fixed rates, turns them into regular data, and sends them to processors built for dense computation.
This mismatch becomes particularly acute in high-speed applications—from autonomous drones to industrial processes such as laser additive manufacturing—where relevant physical dynamics can evolve faster than conventional sensing and processing pipelines can handle.
Sampling fast enough to capture these dynamics produces massive data streams, much of which is irrelevant to the task, making real-time processing increasingly constrained.
Turning sensing into selection
The path from physical sensing to AI needs an intermediate layer—not to process more data, but to select the information worth moving downstream. Neuromorphic principles provide a natural foundation for such a layer.
Event-based sensors turn sensing into selection. They respond to change as it happens, encoding only events that carry new information. An event camera, for example, records changes in light at each pixel, capturing their timing and location without continuously sampling the scene.

articles.title: Beyond the vault: Who's responsible for what banking sites share?

Beyond the vault: Who's responsible for what banking sites share?
Banking sites leak financial data via tracking scripts despite consent
Banks spend heavily to convince customers they are the most careful custodians of personal and financial data.
Our review of 14 financial-services websites across Europe and the US found otherwise: tracking and personalization scripts embedded in account-opening, mortgage, and loan-application flows sent contact details, financial intent, and device fingerprints to third parties, with 9 of the 14 sites doing so without a valid consent choice in place.
Head of Security Research at Jscrambler.
The failures fall into three patterns, and the distinction between them matters legally.
First, tags fired before the cookie banner had been answered at all, on wealth-management, investment-banking, and payment-provider sites; under the EU's ePrivacy Directive, that behavior never had a lawful basis, since consent is required before anything is stored on or read from a device.
Second, tracking continued after a user actively rejected cookies: at one site, Google Ads and DoubleClick still received the user's hashed email in the request URL alongside the consent-denied signal, meaning the rejection was recorded and then ignored.

En 1857, Ignacio Uranga y Nicolasa Montaner compraron 5.000 hectáreas de tierra unos 40 kilómetros al sur de Rosario, Argentina. La idea inicial era criar ovejas; pero, rápidamente, llegaron las vacas y tras ellas el trigo. Para la década de los 80 del siglo XX, la sobrexplotación del terreno empezó a producir algo curioso: con cada temporada de lluvias, el campo perdía tierra superficial. Si no se andaban con cuidado, terminarían arando sobre piedra.
Fue entonces cuando, desesperados, decidieron hacer algo que era considerado todo un anatema: dejaron de arar.
Puede parecer algo minoritario o una excentricidad argentina, peor lo cierto es que llevamos casi 20 años viviendo una silenciosa revolución agrícola en todo el mundo. Ahora parece que están saltando las costuras.
¿Qué es la siembra directa? En el modelo habitual, arar es imprescindible: es un proceso que no solo airea la tierra, sino que acaba con las malas hierbas. En 2007, David Montgomery recopiló datos de medio mundo y llegó a la conclusión de que los campos arados pierden suelo entre diez y cien veces más rápido de lo que somos capaces de regenerarlo. Es decir, el problema no solo ocurre a 40 kilómetros de Rosario.
En este sentido, el modelo de siembra directa ofrece una solución: solo se siega y se planta. El rastrojo permanece en su sitio, amortigua la lluvia, frena la escorrentía y reduce la evaporación. Según los datos de los que disponemos, el ritmo de pérdida de suelo es muy parecido al de la formación.

The Institute for Supply Management reported that its Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index registered 54.5% in September, edging down just 0.1 percentage point from August’s reading of 54.6%. In ISM’s economic modeling, a PMI reading of 54.5% corresponds to a 2.4% annualized increase in real gross domestic product.

articles.title: Siempre se culpa injustamente a Egipto, Italia y Turquía de la cantidad de plástico que tiene el Mediterráneo
articles.summary:
El mar Mediterráneo se ha convertido en un auténtico vertedero de plásticos, y una vez más los humanos somos los responsables de esto. Aquí hay varios posibles culpables, puesto que son muchos los países que tienen un contacto directo con este mar y esto es precisamente lo que los datos tratan de dilucidar.
Lo que se sabe. El dato más repetido a raíz de esta contaminación proviene del informe de la UICN publicado en 2020 y que muchos medios han utilizado para poder señalar a Egipto, Italia y Turquía como los grandes y casi exclusivos culpables del problema. Pero si comenzamos a indagar en los temas no hay que responsabilizar tanto a estos países.
Los datos apuntan a que anualmente vertemos hasta 229.000 toneladas de plástico a nuestro mar, pero con un margen de error amplio y que oscila entre 150.000 y 610.000 toneladas. Pero al final, con lo que nos quedamos es que vertemos una cantidad vertiginosa de plásticos a nuestro mar.
Por países, encontramos que Egipto tira 74.031 toneladas al año, Italia 34.309 toneladas y Turquía 23.966 toneladas. Estos tres países suman algo menos del 58% del total, lo cual dista de ser una mayoría aplastante. Y es que aquí el secreto puede estar en ordenar a los países que más plástico tiran en relación a su población y aquí los mayores emisores pasan a ser Montenegro (con 8,7 kg/año por habitante), seguidos de Albania, Bosnia-Herzegovina y Macedonia del Norte.

The project relinks PS5 executables into the host system's native format and reimplements the console's system libraries for dynamic linking, similar to Wine or Proton. Since the PS5 already runs on x86-64 Zen 2 hardware, which is similar to a modern PC, AnyPS5 skips CPU emulation and recompiles shaders into SPIR-V for Vulkan instead.
What is particularly interesting is that once GPU shader instructions are translated, all the system needs are PS5 libraries so they can be dynamically linked from a native PC port. This means the PS5 game will see the exact same system calls on a PC as it does on the console. However, the system libraries have not yet been fully translated, with current statistics showing 84.81% of system libraries translated. Rajeev Badyal, le responsable du projet Amazon Leo, vient d’accorder une interview très révélatrice à nos confrères d’Ars Technica, aux côtés de deux autres cadres, Paul Palcisco et Chris Weber. Un témoignage qui ne manque pas de sel, puisqu’il a piloté Starlink à ses débuts avant qu’Elon Musk ne l’écarte, le jugeant trop prudent.

After years of volunteering to help others navigate what she had to learn on her own, it occurred to Tashakorinia that AI might be able to help — not with the complex, messy experience of grieving and healing, but with the least human parts of the process, like finding the right tax forms, filing insurance claims, and shutting down bank accounts.
The result is LumenUs, the grief care platform that Tashakorinia founded last year to relieve grieving families of some of the administrative burden.
“I think going through it, your threshold of pain is so high, and you’re so lost that you don’t really realize, why do people treat you this way? Why was I left with a stack of paperwork, and why was the funeral home charging me a 300% markup on a casket?” Tashakorinia said.

Moving AI from pilot to production starts with the data
AI pilots fall down when AI lacks context
AI adoption has moved quickly. McKinsey’s 2025 global survey found that 88% of respondents say their organizations regularly use AI tools in at least one business function, up from 78% the previous year, yet only 7% say AI is fully scaled across the organization, with 30% remaining stuck in the piloting phase.
CEO & Co-Founder at Adverity.
For marketing teams, this gap becomes even more obvious when an AI pilot meets the complexity of the existing data stack. A pilot can demonstrate what an AI model is capable of when it has a defined task and carefully selected data, but moving that capability into a live enterprise environment is often considerably harder.
The issue often sits beneath the model itself. Marketing data is spread across platforms, warehouses and internal systems, with different structures and definitions making it difficult for AI to establish what the numbers actually mean.
The pilot works until it meets the real world
There is a reason AI pilots can look so convincing at the beginning. The scope is usually narrow, the data is easier to control and the questions being asked are relatively straightforward.

Desde compartir una red inalámbrica hasta guardar los primeros pasos de un bebé en video, estos códigos permiten concentrar información dispersa en un solo escaneo.
Usos practicos para los códigos QR

Es por ello que Google DeepMind lanzó SynthID en 2023, una marca y herramienta de uso cerrado para identificar imágenes falsas. Ahora han decidido abrirla a todo el mundo y es más capaz que nunca.
El problema es que está (muy) lejos de ser infalible.
SynthID. Realmente, se trata de la tecnología de marcas de agua que DeepMind lanzó hace varios años y, básicamente, es algo que incrusta una marca imperceptible en imágenes, vídeo, audio o texto generado por IA. Lo hace en el momento de crear la pieza y no es algo que veamos (como una marca de agua en texto o el símbolo de Gemini que antes se introducía en la IA de Google), sino algo más profundo pensado para resistir recortes y filtros por encima en el caso de imágenes, de cambios de fotogramas y compresión con pérdida en vídeo o de ruido, compresión agresiva y cambios de velocidad en el caso del audio.
Según Google, con esta tecnología han marcado más de 180.000 millones de imágenes y vídeos... y más de 240.000 años de audio. Es tan loco el haber marcado eso como que se haya generado tantísimo en tan poco tiempo.

“There's a sort of soullessness to them, and I find it sad that we appear to be increasingly happy to settle for that.”
I'm talking to Rob Biddulph, the children’s book illustrator and author who rose to prominence during the Covid pandemic when his #DrawWithRob YouTube channel racked up millions of views from children and parents needing an outlet for their creativity, about a very different kind of pandemic: the proliferation of AI-generated art.
Biddulph was named Illustrator of the Year 2025 at the British Book Awards, but today he’s talking about the troubling increase he's seeing in shops and cafes and other venues displaying posters that are clearly designed by AI.
“I think they're really depressing, to be honest," he tells me. "One of the things I love about illustration is that it's an expression of somebody's individual personality. Human beings can't help but put a bit of their own personality into a drawing or a design.
"Often, you can look at a piece of artwork and recognize the person who made it — see their quirks, their imperfections, their sense of humor and the decisions they've made along the way. To me, that's what makes it interesting.

articles.title: Why identity needs a heartbeat, not a checkpoint
articles.summary:
Think about what you had to do the last time you needed to prove your identity.
Did you present your ID? Snap a selfie? Pass a liveness check? In most cases of enterprise security, that’s all it takes to pass through. From that point, many systems effectively assume that the person who was verified remains the person controlling the session.
But that’s increasingly not the case.
Identity checks haven’t suddenly stopped working. Rather, fraudsters and criminals have learned to move around them.
VP of Corporate Affairs at AU10TIX.
The fraud moved past the checkpoint
The modern fraud playbook does not necessarily need to defeat the biometric check at the front door. Session-hijacking malware can take over after a legitimate login. Remote-access tools can turn a verified customer’s device into an attacker’s terminal. Fraud operations can even recruit real people to complete onboarding legitimately before handing the authenticated session to somebody else or to automated systems.
At the moment of verification, the identification document, the face and the live person could all be real. The checkpoint was not necessarily defeated – it was made irrelevant because it didn’t establish that the same person it verified remained in control five minutes later. I call this scenario the “tollbooth mentality.” It’s the belief that passing verification at login means a business can trust whatever happens afterward.

La premisa. Speaking at the recent Linux Foundation Open Source Summit, Jamie Thomas, IBM's Chief Client Innovation Officer for Enterprise Security, warned there is “a bit of a tsunami in vulnerability disclosures,” with approximately 66,000 unique entries expected to emerge in 2026 alone.

So, how can the cybersecurity industry possibly keep up with this pace, Thomas asked, especially when the expectations placed on developers and security professionals continues to grow?

Podcast producer Caloroga Media has launched Linnet, a production studio that runs in a web browser with an artificial intelligence assistant built in.
The company developed it from the workflow behind its own short-form podcasts. The platform seeks to take on the stack of separate accounts podcasters keep for scripting, voice work and editing.
On Linnet that work happens in one workspace under a single subscription. Linnet is also the name of the assistant, and Caloroga refers to it as “she.” Before it touches a project, the assistant shows exactly what it plans to do and waits for the creator to approve the change.
“Linnet exists because we could not find a tool worthy of the work,” said Mark Francis, who co-founded Caloroga with John McDermott. Francis said the craft “was missing” from the first wave of AI production tools. He described generating episodes with them, then rebuilding every element by hand in a conventional workstation to get the result to broadcast quality.
The studio Caloroga built in response handles recording and mixing on 24 tracks, with a full plug-in suite. Video podcasts have their own multitrack editor, and scripts can be written in the platform or transcribed from a creator’s existing recordings. articles.title: Endesa destapa fraude eléctrico en 16 restaurantes de Barcelona gracias a una IA y a la promoción de unos influencers
articles.summary:
Hay estrategias de marketing que salen caras, y luego está esta, que la han destapado de la forma más irónica posible. Según El Periódico, dieciséis restaurantes de Barcelona (varios de ellos buffets atiborrados de gente) contrataron a influencers para que les hicieran promoción. Los influencers fueron, comieron, grabaron, etiquetaron y dieron las gracias. Lo que nadie calculó es que ese vídeo de un salón lleno de gente podía acabar delante de un algoritmo con una pregunta poco gastronómica: ¿y esto cuánta luz gasta? Pues, al parecer, mucha más de la que pagaban.
No mires el contador, mira el vídeo. El razonamiento es casi de sentido común. Los locales eran enormes, las redes los mostraban llenos y los datos de consumo eléctrico no cuadraban. Para salir de dudas, varios técnicos de Endesa pasaron el asunto por su propia IA, que cruzó consumo y dimensiones y dictaminó lo evidente: por tamaño y actividad esperable, esos restaurantes deberían estar pagando bastante más.
De hecho, ya detectan enganches ilegales para el cultivo de marihuana mediante su propia herramienta. Poco después, se inspeccionó y a las semanas se documentó el fraude: los locales andaban presuntamente pinchados al alumbrado público. Según fuentes de la Unidad contra el Fraude de Endesa, “Las redes son hoy lo que fue en el pasado la Guía del Ocio de Barcelona”.

articles.title: Identity security for AI agents: 18 insights from Navigate 2026 - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
18 insights from SailPoint’s Navigate event: Enterprises race to bring identity security for AI agents up to machine speed
AI agents have made identity the front line of enterprise security. Agents now number in the thousands. They pick up access nobody meant to give them, and when they’re blocked partway through a task, they look for another way in. That has turned identity security for AI agents into a board-level priority rather than a future project.
The focus has moved from finding agents to acting on what discovery turns up. The next phase will be about remediation at machine speed: just-in-time access instead of standing privilege, a named human owner for every agent and enforcement that sits outside the agent itself.
“We need administrative, we need good compliance controls, but the real issue now … is how do you secure all these identities?” said Mark McClain (pictured), founder and chief executive officer of SailPoint Technologies Inc. “It took a very small amount of analysis for our technical team to go, ‘We can’t do this effectively in quote admin time.’ We have to be in the real-time decision-making cycle of, ‘Is this agent with its context and its intent doing what we expect?'”

articles.title: OpenAI revenue falls short, models play hopscotch and Trump cracks down on tech green cards - SiliconANGLE

OpenAI revenue falls short, models play hopscotch and Trump cracks down on tech green cards
I’m not going to call the bursting of artificial intelligence bubble yet, not with all that money still pouring into every hardware and software company with AI in their pitch decks. But we got a little taste this week.
OpenAI told investors this week that it actually had $18 billion less revenue than the $68 billion it said last month. That knocked down the stocks of Nvidia, CoreWeave, Oracle and Nebius, among others, on Thursday.
Fifty billion dollars in revenue is nothing to scoff at, of course, but the market is all about expectations, and investors are growing increasingly wary — not least because some of the frontier AI model companies such as Anthropic may be getting a little pushback from their biggest customers. And by the way — will this finally put ARR to bed as a metric? Or maybe IPOs to come, with disclosures of real numbers, will make it all moot.
Still, nobody’s slowing down much despite persistent worries about AI’s downsides. Google this week debuted its one-stop Gemini assistant that can act autonomously, generate code and complete work across any device, including web, mobile and desktop. And a bunch of other new models came out from OpenAI, Anthropic and others.

articles.summary:
La campagne MALFEX exploite plusieurs bibliothèques npm pour diffuser des malwares sur Windows. Parmi ses méthodes, deux détournent des fichiers PNG, tantôt en leur empruntant leur apparence, tantôt en y dissimulant des données chiffrées.

La solution tout-en-un pour protéger votre entreprise

Une nouvelle étude signée HEC et la Banque de France vient confirmer ce que beaucoup craignaient. L'IA a déjà commencé son travail de sape dans le monde de l'emploi, et particulièrement du côté des plus fragiles : les jeunes.
Selon cette étude, dont La Croix se fait l'écho, depuis 2022 (moment où l'IA décolle, avec le lancement de ChatGPT en novembre de cette année) les embauches en CDI des 21-29 ans ont lourdement chuté, de 28,3%, dans les emplois les plus exposés. Un recul qui correspond tout simplement à près de 75 000 CDI en moins offerts chaque année à cette classe d'âge.
Un danger à long terme pour les entreprises ?
Et il s'agit de postes non crées, et non pas de basculements de CDI vers des CDD. En effet, tout contrats confondus, le recul reste de 22,1%. À noter que ce que l'étude appelle emplois les plus exposés va de journaliste, traducteur ou technicien d'opérations bancaires à développeur informatiqu…

Les négociations autour du Projet de loi de finances (PLF) 2027 ont débuté, dans une ambiance qui a rarement été aussi rude, au vu des difficultés financières de l'État. Et il semble que personne n'échappera aux envies de taxation des députés, et surtout pas la cible toujours facible des cryptomonnaies. Car un amendement qui vient juste d'être voté va faire parler !

Voilà un amendement qui na va pas plaire à tout le monde ! En effet, l'amendement déposé par le député communiste Nicolas Sansu et imposant la taxation lors d'un passage d'une cryptomonnaie à un stablecoin vient d'être adopté en Commission des finances.
Avec cet amendement, tout passage d'une cryptomonnaie à un stablecoin comme l'USDC déclenche le calcul d'une plus-value. Et si plus-value il y a, celle-ci devient soumise à la flat tax, ou au barème progressif de l'impôt sur le revenu. Aujourd'hui, seul le passage au fiat (comme l'euro) déclenche l'imposition.

Durante este proceso, la cuenta queda suspendida de forma temporal y el usuario no puede enviar ni recibir mensajes, realizar llamadas ni acceder a ninguna de las funciones del servicio.
Aunque el mensaje puede generar preocupación, no significa necesariamente que la cuenta haya sido bloqueada de forma definitiva. La revisión forma parte de los mecanismos de seguridad de WhatsApp para detectar posibles casos de spam, uso de aplicaciones no autorizadas o actividades que infrinjan las políticas de la plataforma. Una vez finalizado el análisis, la cuenta puede ser restablecida si no se detectan incumplimientos.
¿Por qué aparece el mensaje “Cuenta en revisión”?
WhatsApp utiliza sistemas automatizados para identificar comportamientos que puedan representar un riesgo para la seguridad de la plataforma o de otros usuarios.
Una de las causas más frecuentes es el uso de aplicaciones modificadas como WhatsApp Plus, GB WhatsApp u otras versiones no oficiales. Estas aplicaciones alteran el funcionamiento original del servicio y violan las condiciones de uso establecidas por Meta.

El informe analiza las amenazas detectadas entre el 1 de julio de 2025 y el 30 de junio de 2026 y advierte que la inteligencia artificial (IA), el robo de identidades digitales y la conexión entre sistemas y proveedores están cambiando la forma en que se producen los ataques informáticos.
El relevamiento se elaboró a partir del análisis de más de 165 billones de señales de seguridad procesadas diariamente por Microsoft. Entre sus principales conclusiones, destaca que los ciberdelincuentes pueden aprovechar herramientas de IA para acelerar sus operaciones y que el robo de una cuenta puede convertirse en la puerta de entrada a otros sistemas, con consecuencias que se extienden a distintas empresas y sectores.
El reporte también advierte sobre la velocidad de los ataques: el tiempo entre el descubrimiento de una vulnerabilidad y su explotación puede ser inferior a 24 horas. Esto reduce el margen que tienen las organizaciones para actualizar sus sistemas y corregir fallas antes de que sean aprovechadas por los delincuentes.

La particularidad del servicio es que los reportes salen directo del modelo, sin que un humano los revise antes de enviarlos a los equipos de cada proyecto. Anthropic lo reconoce de forma explícita en su comunicado.
“Los resultados de este escáner de vulnerabilidades opcional serán generados íntegramente por el modelo, sin revisión ni clasificación humana”, escribió la empresa, y aclaró que eso implica que algunos reportes podrían ser incorrectos o inválidos.
El cuello de botella que motivó el cambio
Anthropic explicó que durante los últimos seis meses usó sus modelos para escanear software ampliamente utilizado y encontró más de 29.000 vulnerabilidades candidatas. De esa cifra, solo pudo revisar y confirmar manualmente alrededor de 6.000.
La compañía admitió que ese proceso de verificación humana se convirtió en una traba. Por eso, ante el pedido de varios mantenedores de recibir todo lo que el modelo detectaba sin esperar la validación, ya envió cerca de 5.000 reportes sin revisar a quienes lo solicitaron.

The hackers have been breaking into networks since at least mid-January 2021, according to the agencies' joint advisory. It describes the hacking in the present tense but provides no date for any theft and does not specify how many organizations were breached.
The same hackers targeted U.S. government services, critical manufacturing, healthcare, and IT organizations, along with U.S. law enforcement, education, and religious groups. Organizations in Southeast Asia, Africa, and North America were also targeted.
The hackers also run a web application that "provides third-party access to stolen email content," the advisory said. It does not identify those third parties.
In September 2024, the FBI disrupted a botnet, a network of hijacked devices, that the U.S. Justice Department said Integrity Technology Group controlled. It held more than 200,000 routers, cameras, and other consumer devices, and Lumen researchers had named it Raptor Train.

Au rayon connectique, les boîtes se ressemblent toutes, sauf par le prix. L'une promet la "8K", l'autre des "couleurs plus riches", une troisième met en avant ses contacts dorés. Entre la moins chère et la plus chère, le prix est facilement multiplié par dix. Et quand on vient de payer un téléviseur 1 500 €, on est tenté de lui offrir un câble qui semble à sa hauteur.
Des 0 et des 1, rien d'autre
Le HDMI transporte de l'information numérique. La console ou le lecteur envoie une suite de bits, que le téléviseur reçoit pour reconstruire l'image pixel par pixel. Tant que chaque bit arrive tel qu'il est parti, l'écran affiche ce que la source a produit, et un câble plus épais ne peut rien faire pour les couleurs ou le contraste. À l'époque de la péritel ou du VGA, c'était différent : un mauvais cordon analogique délavait réellement l'image.
Quand la liaison numérique faiblit, on le voit tout de suite. Les ingénieurs parlent d'effet falaise : l'image reste parfaite tant que le signal est lisible, puis se dégrade brutalement. articles.title: GoBalance Flaw Lets Attackers Hijack .onion Addresses by Recovering Tor-Format Keys
articles.summary:
A bug in GoBalance, a tool many dark-web sites use to stay reachable during attacks, lets anyone work out the secret key that controls a site's .onion address using only public information, and then take that address over.
Searchlight Cyber, which disclosed the flaw on October 8, says an attacker who recovers the key can redirect the site's visitors to a copy of the site they control. Taking over the address does not grant the attacker access to the site's servers, database, or stored user data.
How the Flaw Works
An .onion address is really a public key, so whoever holds the matching private key controls the address. To stay reachable, a site publishes a signed record, called a descriptor, that anyone on the Tor network can fetch, and GoBalance signs that record.
The flaw is in the signing step. A Tor private key is 64 bytes long, but GoBalance passed only the first 32 bytes to the signer and dropped the rest. The dropped half is the part that keeps each signature's secret value hidden.
Without that half, the secret value becomes a fixed number anyone can compute. A single published descriptor then carries enough to recover the site's private key, with no access to its servers.
Because the exposed key is the site's long-term master key, not a short-lived one, a recovered key can sign valid records for the address far into the future.

The data shows that while businesses have spent years maturing their identity programs for human employees, those same playbooks are fundamentally broken when applied to the ephemeral, autonomous, and rapidly multiplying world of non-human AI agents.
A Market Stalled at the Starting Line

The multi-year persistence of this trend reveals a critical insight: the problem isn't a lack of effort, but an architectural ceiling. The operational playbooks built to govern human employees may not scale effectively to govern autonomous agents executing thousands of transactions per minute.

articles.title: Qué empresas lideraban la venta de celulares al inicio del negocio: quiénes eran los Apple y Samsung de la época
articles.summary:
Durante las décadas de 1980 y 1990, mucho antes de que Apple y Samsung se convirtieran en protagonistas del mercado de los teléfonos inteligentes, otras compañías dominaban la industria de la telefonía móvil.
Motorola, Nokia y Ericsson fueron algunas de las marcas que definieron esa etapa, con equipos que marcaron el paso de los primeros celulares comerciales a dispositivos más compactos, accesibles y preparados para las redes digitales.
Motorola fue una de las grandes pioneras del sector, mientras que Nokia terminó por convertirse en el principal fabricante mundial de teléfonos móviles a finales de los años noventa. Ericsson, por su parte, tuvo un papel relevante tanto en el desarrollo de dispositivos como en la infraestructura que permitió expandir las comunicaciones inalámbricas.
La comparación con Apple y Samsung ayuda a entender la evolución del negocio, aunque el mercado de aquella época era diferente al actual: los celulares se utilizaban principalmente para llamar y enviar mensajes, y el diseño, la autonomía de la batería, la cobertura y la resistencia eran factores decisivos para los compradores.
Motorola, la compañía que abrió el camino
La historia del teléfono móvil comercial está estrechamente vinculada con Motorola, empresa estadounidense que presentó en 1983 el DynaTAC 8000X. articles.title: Anthropic Launches Free AI Vulnerability Scanner for Open-Source Projects
articles.summary:
Anthropic on Thursday unveiled OSS Scanner as an opt-in vulnerability scanner to help secure the open-source ecosystem using artificial intelligence (AI).
"It's an opt-in service informed by our experience using Claude to find vulnerabilities during Project Glasswing," Anthropic said. "Projects that join will receive thorough, periodic security scans by our strongest models at no cost."
Anthropic also noted that the outputs of the scanner will be fully model-generated and do not require human review or triage, thereby facilitating faster and more frequent scanning. These reports are expected to be generated by its strongest models, including Claude Mythos.
The company pointed out that it expects to use a set of criteria similar to Google's OSS-Fuzz to pick projects, while emphasizing that the process may evolve over time. Project maintainers are advised to provide a short description explaining the importance of their project in cases where "it is not already self-evident."
Core maintainers of a project can enroll by opening a pull request on the OSS Scanner's GitHub repository along with a YAML configuration file that provides the following information -
- Link to the git repository that should be cloned
- Email address of the primary contact
- A repository-relative path to the Dockerfile that sets up the environment, pre-installs all dependencies and builds the project so to help an offline agent conduct its security audit

articles.title: Cuáles fueron los primeros celulares comerciales de la historia: top 6 de Nokia 1100 al primer Motorola
articles.summary:
Hubo una época en la que hablar por teléfono en plena calle parecía una escena de ciencia ficción. Hoy, los celulares permiten trabajar, estudiar, tomar fotografías y acceder a internet desde cualquier lugar, pero la historia de estos dispositivos comenzó con equipos voluminosos, costosos y con una autonomía limitada.
En poco más de cuatro décadas, la industria pasó de teléfonos que apenas permitían conversar durante media hora a los smartphones que concentran buena parte de la vida digital.
El primer celular portátil comercial fue el Motorola DynaTAC 8000X, que llegó al mercado estadounidense en 1983. Su desarrollo había comenzado años antes: en 1973, el ingeniero, Martin Cooper, realizó una llamada desde un teléfono móvil experimental.
Este dispositivo comercial pesaba cerca de 800 gramos, medía unos 25 centímetros de alto sin contar la antena y costaba alrededor de 4.000 dólares. Su batería necesitaba aproximadamente diez horas de carga para ofrecer hasta 30 minutos de conversación.
Aquel avance fue posible gracias al despliegue de las primeras redes celulares comerciales. Japón puso en marcha una red en 1979 y los países nórdicos inauguraron el sistema NMT en 1981. Desde entonces, fabricantes como Motorola, Nokia y Siemens compitieron por reducir el tamaño de los equipos y ampliar sus funciones.

articles.title: Researchers Publish Working Exploit for Pre-Auth AnyDesk Linux Flaw That Gives Root Access
articles.summary:
Security researchers have published a full working exploit for a pre-authentication remote code execution flaw in AnyDesk Linux that gives attackers root access before anyone approves the connection.
AnyDesk patched the flaw in version 8.0.3 in June, but its changelog described the fix only as "fixed a bug that could lead to a crash," with no CVE assigned and no security advisory.
The exploit, called AnyPwn, targets a heap buffer overflow in AnyDesk's session protocol, a remote desktop tool. The code was released on GitHub on October 8.
Administrators should update AnyDesk Linux to at least version 8.0.3. The latest release is 8.1.0.
What the Exploit Demonstrates
The published exploit works only over direct TCP connections on port 7070.
The exploit is probabilistic: the heap layout must place a target object adjacent to the overflowed buffer; otherwise, the service crashes instead of executing the attacker's command. The offsets in the published code target a specific build of AnyDesk Linux, 8.0.2; other builds would require different values.
The researchers say the same vulnerable code path is also reachable via AnyDesk's relay servers, which the software uses when a direct connection is unavailable. They validated this with a Frida instrumentation trigger but did not demonstrate the full exploit chain over relays.
AnyDesk said in June that the vulnerability is "limited to direct connections on Linux (connections that do not go through our relays). Windows and macOS are not …

articles.title: TP-Link Sued by Four More U.S. States Over Router Security and China Ties
articles.summary:
Four more U.S. states sued router maker TP-Link Systems on October 6, bringing the total to five, with Texas filing a suit in February. Florida, Iowa, Montana and Nebraska allege the California company misled buyers about how secure its routers are and how separate it is from China. TP-Link denies the claims and says it will fight them in court.
TP-Link Systems is based in Irvine, California. Until a 2024 restructuring, it was affiliated with TP-Link Technologies, a Chinese company that the suits do not name as a defendant.
The complaints from Florida, Montana , and Nebraska do not allege that the Chinese government has obtained customers' data through TP-Link. They describe that as a risk under Chinese law. Separately, they say state-backed hackers have exploited flaws in TP-Link routers.
Iowa's announcement is worded more strongly in places. Attorney General Brenna Bird's office said TP-Link firmware gives the Chinese government access to Iowans' devices and data. The same release also describes that access as something that could happen.
The next day, 21 state attorneys general sent a letter to the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) about TP-Link's effort to win approval for new router models in the U.S.
Three of the complaints also cite five flaws in TP-Link devices supplied by internet service providers (ISPs) to customers. Researchers published technical details of those flaws on October 8. Fixes exist, and they reach users through their ISP.

articles.title: P7 DarkSword iOS Exploit Kit Adds Crypto Wallet Data Theft and Remote Commands
articles.summary:
Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a previously unseen variant of the DarkSword iOS exploit kit called P7 DarkSword.
"Compared with the variants we usually observe, P7 reduces its on-device footprint, adds on-device keychain and crypto-wallet theft, and adds two way C2 communication with the attacker's infrastructure," iVerify said in a new report published Thursday.
The name "P7" is a nod to the threat actor's use of the "p7_" variable prefix in changes made to the original DarkSword code.
DarkSword was first publicly documented earlier this March by Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG), iVerify, and Lookout, detailing its ability to target iPhones running iOS versions between iOS 18.4 and 18.7. The kit was detected in the wild in November 2025.
The toolkit is engineered to chain multiple iOS vulnerabilities to escape the browser sandbox, escalate to kernel privileges, and inject the main payload into SpringBoard, the iOS process that handles app launches and the home screen. The exploit chain is assessed to be a commercial product that somehow landed in a second-hand market, from where it was acquired by financially motivated operators and other threat actors since late 2025.
The exploit kit has been put to use in attacks targeting Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Malaysia, and Ukraine by multiple threat actors, including a Turkish commercial surveillance vendor named PARS Defense via a fake Snapchat-themed website and a Russia-aligned threat actor called Star Bliz…

articles.title: FBI Arrests Another ShinyHunters Suspect Reportedly Involved in Its Jobs Portal Hack
articles.summary:
The FBI has arrested another suspected co-conspirator of ShinyHunters, FBI Director Kash Patel said on October 9 in a post on X.
ShinyHunters is the extortion group that said in September it had breached the FBI's jobs portal and stolen sensitive data on almost all FBI agents and job applicants. The FBI has not named the suspect, and no charges have been made public.
The suspect is a Canadian citizen who was arrested in Pennsylvania, according to The New York Times and CBS News. Both cited unnamed sources.
The Times reported that the arrest was made on suspicion of involvement in the theft of FBI data. A law enforcement source told CBS News that the suspect is believed to have been directly involved in the hack.
An FBI spokesperson declined to comment on the Times report, CBS News said. Patel's post does not say whether the suspect took part in the breach. It calls ShinyHunters "the group believed to be responsible for the recent FBIjobs.gov incident."
Patel also wrote that the FBI will keep working with its partners "to disrupt what’s left of the ShinyHunters group and their associates, no matter where they operate." Other suspected co-conspirators are still free, the law enforcement source told CBS News.
Earlier Arrests in the Netherlands and Jordan

articles.summary:
Scalpers from the US are not the only players looking to score a piece of the .si domain gold rush — but the country dominating the list might surprise you
Here is who is really buying "super intelligence" domains
- Register.si logged 19,541 new .si names in 24 hours, about five times its pre-order daily pace
- India (3,174) edged the US (3,135) in Hostinger's data, with Morocco a surprising third on 678
- Hostinger handled roughly two in five new .si names on September 30 and October 1 2026, and says its sales peaked October 5 before cooling to about 4x pre-order levels
The scramble for Slovenia's .si domain has not burned out just yet: on October 9 2026, the live counter on the Register.si homepage showed 19,541 new .si names registered in the preceding 24 hours.
This is roughly five times the average of about 3,700 a day the registry logged in the week between President Trump's UN speech and his executive order.
The usual assumption would be that this is an American land grab of virtual real estate, but data from Hostinger, one of the biggest retail sellers of the extension, complicates that picture considerably: across the nine days its dashboard covers, customers in India registered 3,174 .si names against 3,135 from the US, a gap of just 39 even as Morocco comes a distant third.
